image_description: A large, dark wood built-in bookcase spanning a wall in a room. The unit features multiple vertical sections with adjustable shelves filled with books and decorative items. The top of the bookcase is adorned with greenery. To the left, a black chair and a framed picture are visible on the adjacent wall.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular furniture piece of considerable height, notably taller than wide.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The structure is clearly a tall, rectangular unit extending vertically across most of the frame height.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tall rectangular frame with horizontal divisions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bookcase has distinct vertical stiles and horizontal shelves creating a grid-like frame structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bilateral symmetry with open front displaying books and objects.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While individual bays may be symmetrical, the overall unit is asymmetrical due to the varying widths of the sections (left narrow, middle wide, right medium) and the different contents on each shelf.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Multiple horizontal shelves spaced evenly from top to bottom.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Each vertical section contains multiple horizontal shelves holding books, spaced relatively evenly.
Adjustability is an internal mechanical feature not visually verifiable from this distance without seeing pin holes or brackets clearly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some models have glass doors on upper section.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This specific model appears to be open-shelf; no glass doors are visible on any section.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood particleboard or metal with finished surface stained painted or laminated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface has a dark stain finish consistent with wood or wood veneer.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Front open displaying books and objects on each shelf.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The shelves are openly accessible and filled with books and various decorative objects.
The finish is smooth and reflective; while explicit hardware like knobs is minimal/absent, the trim and molding act as decorative elements.

artifact_observations.location: Book spines on middle and lower shelves
artifact_observations.reasoning: Text on book spines is largely illegible or nonsensical upon close inspection, typical of AI generation where text rendering fails at small scales.
The plants on top of the bookcase lack distinct leaf definition and appear slightly smudged or painterly compared to the sharp geometry of the shelves.
The baseboard interaction and the very bottom edge of the rightmost column appear slightly soft and indistinct, blending into the carpet/shadow area.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a bookcase and not a generic cabinet or shelving unit.
To verify the 3D consistency of the shelves and ensure books sit correctly within the depth of the shelves without floating.
To check for boundary bleeding between books and shelves, and ensure individual books are distinct entities.
To assess the severity of the text gibberish and texture anomalies noted in the initial scan.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of text on book spines
Geometric alignment of vertical stiles and horizontal shelves
Boundary separation between books and shelf surfaces
Texture consistency of wood grain vs. background walls
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact on the book spines. While common in AI images, evaluate if it disrupts the realism significantly. Also, verify if the 'asymmetry' noted in checkpoints is a defect or just a design choice of this specific built-in unit. Check if the plant texture anomaly suggests broader generative issues.
